findings.summary: cross_check does not require the six producers to share source, runtime, interpreter, runtime_versions or training_pool. The directive asks for runtime equivalence across all six producers.
findings.trigger: A producer registration whose source_manifest_sha256 or runtime_manifest_sha256 differs from the others (or a different interpreter or training pool). verify_producer returns these values (merge.py:62-63) but cross_check never compares them.
findings.consequence: The merge accepts a mixed-runtime six-model table and publishes it as one fixed-runtime comparison. Current data is uniform (producer source a29e25b285d2..., runtime e032a5ab1d60..., one interpreter), so this is a missing guard, not a present error.
findings.fix: Add equality asserts for producer_source_manifest_sha256, producer_runtime_manifest_sha256, interpreter, runtime_versions and training_pool_sha256 across the six in cross_check, plus a merge_tests case that mutates one producer. Re-seal and rebuild the draft if this lands before source acceptance.

findings.summary: The merge fixtures use a constant shift per pair (DELTAS), so every bootstrap interval collapses to low == high == delta. The stored-interval reproduction and the shared-index resampling are therefore not exercised on non-degenerate data.
findings.trigger: Real per-seed variation in which merge.bootstrap (merge.py:200-225) and paired_statistics.paired_intervals consume the RNG or sort in a different order.
findings.consequence: The merge refuses at check_against_stored (merge.py:228-234) after both parts are spent. The result is fail-closed (no wrong table is published), but the final output is blocked until a debug cycle.
findings.fix: Add a deterministic per-seed-varying fixture (for example seeded integer noise on the opening_priority arm). Assert that pair-1 and pair-3 merge intervals equal the part-stored intervals with nonzero width, and add a tamper case for the first-part stored interval, since test_stored_part_interval_mismatch_refused edits only the last part.

findings.summary: test_real_accepted_producer_chains_pass_hash_only pins audit hashes for only two of the three last-part producers (replica-3-opening_priority is unpinned) and silently continues when an audit file is missing.
findings.trigger: An audit file is deleted or replaced for replica-3-opening_priority, or any listed audit is replaced. The test still passes as long as at least two producers were checked (checked >= 2).
findings.consequence: The real-chain test is weaker than its name. All six audits exist now, so the gap is in the test, not the data.
findings.fix: Pin the replica-3-opening_priority audit sha256 too, and assert that all three layouts exist instead of continuing.

findings.summary: README and package-manifest describe the pre-audit state, and the README skip claim is false.
findings.trigger: README line 34 says two sealed-package tests skip until sealing. The run has 0 skipped because source-manifest.json exists, so FullRegistrationPath runs (tests.py:651-656). README Activation step 1 and package-manifest readiness_at_preparation and unresolved_blockers still say replica-3-opening_priority is training and no draft exists; all six audits are accepted and the draft exists.
findings.consequence: Stale claims in the reviewed package. Nothing in code depends on them, but a reader would conclude the package is not yet built.
findings.fix: Update README and package-manifest. package-manifest is not pinned by the draft, so it can be fixed without a rebuild. README is a source-manifest member, so editing it needs a re-seal and draft rebuild, and should land in the same pass as F1-F3.

findings.summary: The 3x factor is calibrated against the older seven-policy run. The most recent measured rate (the accepted first part) is about 1.95x slower per raw frame, so the effective margin over that rate is about 1.54x, not 3x.
findings.trigger: Prior run: 684.92 s / 15,487,746 raw frames = 44.2 us/frame. First part: 579.87 s / 6,720,672 raw frames = 86.3 us/frame. Scaled to RAW_CAP (55,335,936) the first-part rate gives about 4,775 s against the 7,352 s work limit.
findings.consequence: No launch blocker: the expected run is about 10 minutes, so the 7,352 s hard stop is generous. If it does trip, the single attempt is spent (fail-closed). The parent should record the effective margin in calibration acceptance.
findings.fix: None required. Record the effective margin (about 1.54x against the first-part rate) in calibration acceptance, or raise the factor if the parent wants 3x against the latest rate.
